\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{चाखणे} (cākhṇe)}{चाखणे (cākhṇe)}]{\mr{चाखणे} (cākhṇe) — to taste}

\label{lesson:MR-C157-cakhne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to bite, then the Marathi for to swallow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{चाखणे}}
\textbf{\mr{चाखणे}} — \emph{cākhṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to taste\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{चाखणे}} (\emph{cākhṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*cakṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}tastes\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 4557).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पेरणे} (perṇe)}{पेरणे (perṇe)}]{\mr{पेरणे} (perṇe) — to sow}

\label{lesson:MR-C157-perne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to swallow, then the Marathi for to taste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पेरणे}}
\textbf{\mr{पेरणे}} — \emph{perṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to sow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पेरणे}} (\emph{perṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{prakirati}, \textquotedblleft{}scatters\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8443). CDIAL glosses the Marathi verb \textquotedblleft{}to scatter, strew, sow\textquotedblright{}, and calls Bloch's source \emph{pradara} wrong.
\end{cousinweb}
